content:
maya: heads up — after the 2026-03 canary i’m seeing a bunch of staging logs with NO request id. quick sample:
```
INFO 2026-03-14T15:02:11Z user=alice action=generate msg='starting'
INFO 2026-03-14T15:02:11Z action=tokenize msg='ok'
INFO 2026-03-14T15:02:12Z msg='finished'
```
no reqid field at all (used to be req_id=...)

kevin: hmm, did we change the otel/autoinit order in the sdk lately? last time this happened the log hook ran before the reqid middleware so logs emitted during init lost the header.

sam: i noticed something similar but only on node sampleapp. go sampleapp still shows reqid. so might be SDK parity issue — node's autoinit sequence fires the otel sampler AFTER the log hooks, and our reqid lives on the context that sampler sometimes drops.

amelia: concrete hypothesis: the otel sampler is returning Drop for internal health-check spans (or at TRACE level), and our reqid middleware is attached as an OTEL hook that depends on span/context to propagate. if the sampler marks span dropped, ctx doesn't get reqid attached before logger runs.

maya: also saw some truncated reqids that look like redaction ate them: e.g. req:_____________. regex in redactor might be too greedy and matching our UUID pattern when loglevel bumps to DEBUG (we attach more metadata and redactor triggers). haven't confirmed yet.

kevin: quick workaround — set REDWOOD_REQID_FALLBACK=true in staging to synthesize a reqid at logger level if none found. but we should fix ordering.

sam: repro steps i used (node sampleapp):
1) checkout branch `fix/reqid-init-order`
2) set OTEL_SAMPLER_PROBABILITY=0.0 and LOG_LEVEL=info
3) run `node ./dist/server.js` and curl /health rapidly
observed missing reqids ~20% of the time during bootstrap.

amelia: possible fixes:
- move reqid hook earlier, before otel autoinit
- make reqid attachment independent of sampler (attach to raw request metadata first)
- make redactor less greedy for our reqid pattern (use word boundaries)

maya: i started a tiny patch that moves the reqid attach to the very first logging hook in node and adds a test in sampleapp that asserts every log line has a reqid header during startup. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/pull/432 (WIP)

kevin: nice. can you also add a small e2e that toggles OTEL_SAMPLER_PROBABILITY to 0 and 1 to ensure parity? Node + Go + python would be ideal but node at minimum.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled to staging at 2026-03-14T15:10:00Z for branch fix/reqid-init-order

sam: FYI i dug into the redactor regex — it was `([A-F0-9]{8}-[A-F0-9\-]{20,})` (case-sensitive) which will happily match parts of some compact reqids when logs are chunked. i suggested switching to `\b[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}\b` and adding an allowlist for traceparent-like strings.

amelia: if we change regex please add a migration note for customers that rely on the old redactor behavior (some stakeholders used the old rule to mask custom tokens).

maya: action items: 1) sam/amelia land the reqid hook reorder + tests (PR 432), 2) kevin add sampler-probability e2e matrix, 3) sam update redactor regex and add allowlist + docs. i'll open a short incident ticket and ping customer-success in case anyone hit by this.

kevin: tl;dr: ordering + sampler interplay caused intermittent loss, and redaction regex exacerbated truncation. patching hook order + safer regex should stop it. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — will monitor staging after canary and post results here. :eyes:
